summary: Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Osaka City University, the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, the University of Hawaiʻi (MA), and Duke University (PhD under Richard M. Jaffe), also studying under Helen Baroni, Michel Mohr, and Amy L. Allocco.

Matthew T. Kapstein specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from UC Berkeley and Brown University, studying under Roderick M. Chisholm, Philip L. Quinn, and others. He held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Matthias de Vries was a Dutch scholar in linguistics. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1838 to 1843, and held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer was a linguist who studied at the University of Graz and earned his PhD from FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, learning under Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held professorships at the universities of Freiburg, Würzburg, and Munich.

Matthieu Ricard is active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a doctorate in molecular biology at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob and studied under traditional teachers Kangyur Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse. He is a Mind & Life Institute board member.

Mattia Salvini specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and SOAS (PhD under Tadeusz Skorupski), also learning under Ram Shankar Tripathi and K. Srinivasan. He held posts at Mahidol University and International Buddhist College.

Mauli Chand Prasad works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as a Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).
Maureen L. P. Patterson was a scholar in Indology who served as South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago, attested in 1984 and 2007.

Maurice Bloomfield was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Chicago, South Carolina, Furman, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and Johns Hopkins (PhD under Charles Rockwell Lanman). He was a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Grammont was a French linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1888–1892) under Ferdinand de Saussure. He subsequently held a post at the University of Montpellier from circa 1895 to 1939.
Maurice Jametel worked in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École des Langues Orientales from circa 1874 to 1878 and later held a post there from circa 1886 to 1889.
Maurice O'Connell Walshe was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula and held a post at the University of London from circa 1948 to 1963.

Maurice Wiles was a religious studies scholar who studied at Christ's College and Ridley Hall, Cambridge. He served at Ridley Hall, University of Ibadan, Clare College, and King's College London, before becoming Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford (1970–1991).

Maurine Stuart worked in Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Manitoba, as well as under Nadia Boulanger, Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, Eido Tai Shimano, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Mauro Maggi completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Naples "L'Orientale." He held posts at the University of Hamburg (1990), IsMEO, and the Istituto Italiano per l'Africa e l'Oriente, and was attested at the University of Rome in 2018.

Mavis L. Fenn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the Universities of Winnipeg, Calgary, and McMaster (PhD under Graeme MacQueen). She held posts at St. Paul's University College and the University of Waterloo.

Max Deeg completed his Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He served as Head of School of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University, attested between 2010 and 2021.

Max Leopold Margolis was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia University and held posts at Columbia, Hebrew Union College, the University of California, Berkeley, and the chair of biblical philology at Dropsie College (1909–1932).
Max Lindenau studied at the University of Leipzig until 1913, where he was a student under Ernst Windisch.

Max Oidtmann specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark Elliott. He held academic posts at Georgetown University in Qatar (2013–2021) and the University of Munich (circa 2021).
